messages:
ashley: heads up — aps5a-rack7-node03 just OOM'd and then hit a SIGBUS while running an active LLM shard. nvml reports a bunch of corrected ECC then an uncorrectable: `GPU 3: ECC uncorrectable, GPU halted`. I'm starting a drain. @kevin can you confirm whether this looks like a convertible HW failure or something softwarey?
sre-bot: ALERT: node=aps5a-rack7-node03 severity=critical metric=nvml_ecc_ue rate=high action=auto-drain initiated_by=policy-evac
kevin: @ashley thanks. Can you paste the kernel oops and dmesg tail? Also what's the job distribution (latency vs batch) on that node right now?
ashley: dmesg snippet pasted: ```[ 123456.789012] NVRM: GPU at 00000000:3:00.0: Xid (SIGBUS): 79, pid=22432, ip=0x7fabc1234, fault: 0x8c01``````[ 123456.790000] EDAC MC0: ECC Error detected on GPU#3: uncorrectable```` Jobs: 4 shards: 2 realtime shards (low-latency), 6 batch jobs draining now (started `gpu-manager drain node=aps5a-rack7-node03 --grace=60s`).
marco: re: capacity — aps5a is pretty tight this week. I'm shifting low-priority batch queues to ap-sg-fallback pool and enabling extra burst nodes in eu-west as a temporary move. Doing `fleetctl reroute --from=aps5a --to=eu-west --tag=batch --max-100` now. Expect some spot churn.
yana: I'll RMA the chassis on rack7. Looks like GPU slot 3 on server03 is consistently failing ECC self-tests. Ordering a replacement board and scheduling chassis swap. ETA hardware on-site ~ 26 hrs. I'll coordinate with ops for a hot-swap window. :wrench: @ops_jun can you reserve a tech?
ops_jun: booked tech for next-day SLA window. I'll also ensure we have spare NVMe sleds and thermal pads in the kit.
kevin: Confirmed logs show repeated Xid=79 and PCIe AER reported multiple fatal errors. Running nvml diag: `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,FB Memory, BAR1` shows persistent FB corruption on GPU3. This is hardware. Keep node drained and mark as DO_NOT_SCHEDULE in cluster: `kubectl label node aps5a-rack7-node03 redwood/maintenance=evacuate` then `kubectl cordon aps5a-rack7-node03`.
ashley: done: cordoned + label applied. Also disabled KV cache warmups for shards that were pinned to that node to avoid cold-start penalty.
marco: Traffic plan: 1) realtime: failover to aps5a-hotspare pool within the region. 2) latency-sensitive customers will be routed to dedicated proxies in eu-central for 10-15% higher p99 but preserved SLA. 3) batch: throttle to 50% and reroute remaining to eu-west. I'll post routing update to incidents channel for downstream teams.
sre-bot: ACTION: autoscaler triggered add_instances region=eu-west count=4 type=gpu-a100-40gb reserved_ttl=3h reason=aps5a_evacuate
yana: ops checklist: 1) RMA order placed 2) tech reserved 3) spare GPU board on-hand 4) schedule window = tomorrow 09:00-11:00 local 5) post-swap diagnostics run (full ECC sweep + memtest).
kevin: for postmortem data, capture: ECC corrected/uncorrected counts, Xid history, thermal history, PCIe AER logs, and the exact model/firmware of the GPU. Tag node with `hw-failure/slot3-gpu` in inventory. Also export the corrupted core dump from /var/crash and upload to s3://redwood-infra-debug/aps5a/rack7/node03/22432.dmp
ashley: uploading logs now. small note: observed higher ambient temp in rack7 shelf B — fans spun to 92%. Could be a thermal exacerbation. Adding to ops ticket.
marco: cost note — moving batch to eu-west + spinning 4 burst nodes will add ~2.4k USD/day if sustained. I'm capping at 3h of burst by autoscaler tag TTL. If we need longer, we should authorize additional spend. @finance FYI.
ops_jun: confirmed thermal sensor in rack7B is 3C above baseline. Tech will check airflow during swap.
yana: after swap we'll run `gpu-sanity --full --repeat=10 --watchdog` before putting node back into rotation. If any ECC uncorrectable shows, we RMA the entire chassis, not just board.
ashley: end state for now: node drained & cordoned, traffic rerouted (realtime -> hotspare, batch -> eu-west throttled), chassis swap scheduled, logs uploaded. Will open an incident ticket with timeline and link to logs.
kevin: thumbs up. Once swap completes, please post the `nvidia-smi -q` output and results of the ECC sweep. We'll reconvene in thread if any regression. :thumbsup:
